| NFR-023 | Domain enums whose labels are user-facing follow the configurable id↔value table pattern: declared in YAML as `[{id, value, default?, color?}, …]`, persisted by id, code references the integer handle only, and an instance-scoped `*domain.EnumRegistry` resolves labels at the DTO boundary. `app.ConfigService.Import` (called from both composition roots — `internal/cli/root.go`, `internal/agentruntime/runtime.go`) returns the registry between `LoadBundle` and `ImportBundle`; every service that touches priority/severity labels (`TaskService`, `LawService`, `WorkflowService`, `TUIQueryService`, `ContextService`, agent `Service`) receives it via constructor. There are no process-global enum registries — `MarshalJSON` / `UnmarshalJSON` on `domain.Priority` and `domain.Severity` have been removed, wire format is the raw int id, and label projection happens at DTO boundaries (e.g. `agent.TaskSummary.Priority` is the resolved label string). Currently applied to `config.priorities` (tasks) and `config.severities` (laws). Validator enforces positive unique ids, unique values, ≤1 default, and ascending declaration order so SQL sort weight matches author intent. | `internal/config/bundle.go` (`PriorityDefinition`, `SeverityDefinition`), `internal/domain/registry.go` (`EnumRegistry`), `internal/app/config_service.go:Import` (returns the registry), `migrations/015_priority_id.sql`, `migrations/016_severity_id.sql`, `.docs/configuration-guide.md#configpriorities`, `.docs/configuration-guide.md#configseverities` |
| NFR-026 | **Architectural rule — config is the single source of truth**: every user-tunable parameter MUST come from `defaults/config/omakase.yaml` (the canonical kit embedded via `go:embed`, materialized into the user's config root alongside the other official presets — `izakaya.yaml`, `kaiseki.yaml`, `shokunin.yaml` — by `EnsureDefaultFiles` on first run). NO canonical default value may live in code as a literal or constant. Concretely: (1) no `Default*` constants, no `Canonical*` slices, no inline literals (`= 500`, `"PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000"`, `map[string]string{"golang": "go", …}`, etc.) for fields that the user could legitimately want to tune; (2) the strict validator (`internal/config/validator.go`) rejects any bundle missing a required field with a message pointing back at the canonical kit; (3) when a Store-level / Service-level knob needs to flow into runtime state, the composition root resolves it from the loaded bundle and writes it via the appropriate setter — never via a code-side fallback. The exhaustive set of currently-required blocks is `kit`, `version`, `config.{output, context, workflow, theme, template_defaults, mcp.*, tui.token_badge.*, views.*, sqlite.busy_timeout_ms, activity_log.{max_rows, max_age_days}, solutions.{default_top_limit, max_top_limit}, events.default_recent_limit, search.stopwords, tag_synonyms, priorities, severities}`, and `workflows[]`. Adding a new tunable to the codebase requires (a) a new field in `config.Settings`, (b) a `validateXSettings` rejecting omission/zero, (c) a value in the kit YAML, (d) a merge entry in `internal/testfixtures/load.go` so partial fixtures inherit it, and (e) wire-up in the composition roots. Defensible-as-code categories explicitly carved out from this rule: protocol allowlists (`asc`/`desc`, sort fields, source enums), correctness PRAGMAs (`foreign_keys=ON`, `journal_mode=WAL`, `synchronous=NORMAL`), file modes (`0o755`/`0o600`), TUI design dimensions, reserved protocol keys (`global`, `---`), and algorithmic heuristics (similar-task `score >= 0.5`, tokenizer `len(word) < 3`, metrics correlation window). Mechanical guard: migration 017 dropped the SQL `DEFAULT` on `tasks.priority_id` and `laws.severity_id` so any code path writing without an explicit config-resolved id fails at the storage layer. Verification path: `grep -rn -E "^\s*(const\|var)\s+[A-Za-z_]+\s*=\s*[0-9]" internal/ \| grep -v _test.go \| grep -v internal/tui/` returns 0 results in production code. | `defaults/config/omakase.yaml`, `internal/config/bundle.go` (no `Default*`/`Canonical*` for tunables), `internal/config/validator.go` (`validateMCPSettings`, `validateTUISettings`, `validateRequiredSort`, `validateSQLiteSettings`, `validateActivityLogSettings`, `validateSolutionsSettings`, `validateEventsSettings`, `validateSearchSettings`, `validateTagSynonyms`, `validatePriorities`, `validateSeverities`), `internal/config/kit.go` (reads `config/omakase.yaml` from the embed), `internal/app/config_service.go:Import` (returns `*domain.EnumRegistry`), `internal/sqlite/store.go` (`ApplyConfig`, `SetActivityLogRetention`, `SetEventsRecentLimit`), `internal/app/error_service.go` (`SetSolutionsDefaults`), `internal/app/tag_normalization.go` (`RegisterTagSynonyms`), `internal/agent/service_helpers.go` (`RegisterStopWords`), `internal/agentruntime/runtime.go`, `internal/cli/root.go`, `internal/testfixtures/load.go` (`mergeKitDefaults`), `migrations/017_drop_priority_severity_defaults.sql` |
| NFR-024 | MCP response-shape limits (`recent_comment_limit`, `recent_context_limit`, `next_work_limit`, `similar_task_limit`, `max_comment_chars`, `include_workflow_in_continue`, `cache_prompts`) are all driven by `config.mcp.*` and pushed into `agent.ServiceSettings` by the composition root via `Service.SetSettings`. The agent layer carries no hardcoded payload caps; validator guarantees every field is set in the bundle, so `Effective*` accessors are identity passthroughs kept only for explicit naming at call sites. | `internal/config/bundle.go` (`MCPSettings`, `Effective*`), `internal/agent/service.go` (`ServiceSettings`, `SetSettings`), `internal/agentruntime/runtime.go`, `internal/cli/root.go` |

## Business Rules

| ID | Rule | Source files |
|----|------|-------------|
| BR-001 | Workflow transitions must be explicitly defined; arbitrary bucket moves are blocked | `internal/app/workflow_service.go:MoveTask`, `internal/sqlite/workflows.go:TransitionAllowed` |
| BR-002 | Workflow guards (e.g., comment-tag presence, blocker buckets) must be satisfied before a move | `internal/app/workflow_service.go`, `internal/sqlite/guards.go`, `internal/sqlite/comments.go` |
| BR-003 | Task dependencies cannot form cycles | `internal/graph/dependency.go:HasCycle`, `internal/app/dependency_service.go` |
| BR-004 | Task dependencies cannot cross projects | `internal/sqlite/dependencies.go:AddTaskDependency`, `internal/app/dependency_service.go` |
| BR-005 | Entity slugs are immutable — renaming requires delete and re-add | `internal/app/bundle_editor.go`, `internal/config/saver.go` |
| BR-006 | Law scope (`global` / `persona` / `project`) is determined by where the slug is referenced in the wiring file | `internal/config/loader_pick.go`, `internal/config/loader_refs.go` |
| BR-007 | Context dump level 1 includes context entries (under the token budget) | `internal/app/context_service.go` |
| BR-008 | Level 2 additionally includes the active workflow, tasks, and dependencies | `internal/app/context_service.go` |
| BR-009 | Level 3 additionally includes comments and active laws | `internal/app/context_service.go` |
| BR-010 | Context content is added newest-first and stops as soon as the budget is exhausted (`Truncated` flag set) | `internal/app/context_service.go` (`contextBudget`) |
| BR-011 | Persona skills are resolved by slug reference and linked via a junction table | `internal/sqlite/personas.go`, `internal/sqlite/bundles.go` |
| BR-012 | The active workflow is determined by the `workflow.active` setting matching a workflow key | `internal/sqlite/workflows.go:ActiveWorkflow` |
| BR-013 | The default bucket for new tasks is the first bucket of the active workflow when no bucket is specified (no hard-coded `backlog`) | `internal/app/workflow_service.go:ResolveDefaultBucket` |
| BR-027 | CRUD policy resolves per `(bucket, entity, op)` via the chain: bucket override → comment-from-task at bucket → workflow.defaults → comment-from-task at defaults → implicit `true`. The first non-`nil` value wins; a missing rule means "allowed". | `internal/domain/workflow.go:resolveBool` |
| BR-028 | Edit on an archived task is rejected with `validation_error` ("task is archived; unarchive before editing"); move on an archived task is similarly blocked. Archive bypasses bucket permissions and transition guards but still respects `operations.archive.guards`. | `internal/app/task_service.go:Edit`, `internal/app/workflow_service.go:MoveTask` |
| BR-029 | Hard delete cascades in this order: comments → event_tags → events → dependencies → tags → task. The `task.removed` event carries a pre-delete snapshot for audit. | `internal/sqlite/tasks_lifecycle.go:HardDeleteTask` |
| BR-014 | Task priority must match an id declared in `config.priorities`. The kit ships `{1=low, 2=normal default, 3=high}`; users may rename, reorder, add, or remove entries. Validator enforces unique ids, unique values, positive ids, ≤1 `default: true` entry, and ascending id order. Same rules apply to `config.severities` (kit ships `{1=info, 2=warning default, 3=error}`) for law severity. | `internal/domain/task.go`, `internal/domain/entities.go`, `internal/config/validator.go` (`validatePriorities`, `validateSeverities`), `internal/config/bundle.go` (`PriorityDefinition`, `SeverityDefinition`, `EffectivePriorities`, `EffectiveSeverities`) |
| BR-015 | Task creation via `tasks.create_intent` requires confirmation when similar or related work already exists | `internal/agent/service_tasks.go:CreateTaskIntent` |
| BR-016 | Dependency removal via agent intent requires explicit `confirmed=true` | `internal/agent/service_dependencies.go:RemoveDependency` |
| BR-017 | Tag removal via agent intent requires explicit `confirmed=true` | `internal/agent/service_tags.go` |
| BR-018 | Agent intents resolve project via standard precedence: explicit `project_id`, explicit `project` slug, then current working directory | `internal/agent/service.go` (`ProjectSelector`), `internal/project/resolver.go` |
| BR-019 | Agent intents must never mix data from different projects | `internal/agent/service_test.go` (e.g., `TestOverviewUsesResolvedProjectAndCompactState`, `TestResumeProjectDoesNotMixProjectState`) |
| BR-020 | Activity logs are pruned synchronously after each insert to cap storage; the bound is `config.activity_log.{max_rows, max_age_days}` (kit canonical: 500 rows / 7 days) | `internal/sqlite/activity_logs.go:BeginActivityLog`, `internal/sqlite/activity_logs.go:PruneActivityLogs`, `internal/sqlite/store.go:SetActivityLogRetention`, `defaults/config/omakase.yaml:config.activity_log` |
| BR-021 | Tag names are normalized to kebab-case and deduplicated on creation | `internal/app/tag_normalization.go`, `internal/app/tag_service.go`, `internal/sqlite/tags.go:FindOrCreateTag` |
| BR-022 | Errors and solutions are cross-project (visible globally) so the agent can reuse prior fixes; only `solutions.confirm(success=true)` increments a solution's like counter | `internal/agent/service_errors.go`, `internal/sqlite/errors.go` |
| BR-023 | The MCP-supported harnesses are exactly `claude-code`, `claude-desktop`, and `opencode`; unsupported values are rejected | `internal/agentsetup/setup.go` (`SupportedHarnesses`) |
| BR-024 | Every MCP tool call must carry a non-empty top-level `_agent_model`; the adapter rejects calls missing it with `validation_error` (system-internal `ReadResource` is exempt and writes empty attribution) | `internal/mcp/adapter.go:extractAgentAttribution`, `internal/mcp/adapter.go:CallTool` |
| BR-025 | `metrics.summary` excludes rows with empty `agent_model` (TUI human, system internals); `search_before_record_ratio` is computed only over records carrying a non-empty `agent_session_id` (correlating searches across parallel agents would inflate the ratio) | `internal/sqlite/metrics.go:AgentMetricsSummary`, `internal/sqlite/metrics.go:fillSearchBeforeRecord` |
| BR-026 | `templates.show` rejects with `validation_error` when the requested slug is a global template shadowed by a project-scoped override of the same `default` kind in the active project; the rejection's `details` carry `requested_slug`, `active_slug`, and `project` so callers re-call directly. Calls outside any registered project preserve the legacy slug-only lookup; an explicit `project`/`project_id` that does not resolve propagates `project_not_found`. | `internal/agent/service_templates.go:ShowTemplate`, `internal/agent/template_test.go` |
| BR-030 | Plan claim is ownership-only. `Store.ClaimNextPlanTask` (and every caller stacked on top of it — `PlanService.ClaimNext`, MCP `plans.claim_next`, `okt plan claim`) only writes `tasks.assigned_to` and emits `task.assigned` inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`; `tasks.bucket_id` is never touched by the claim path. Subsequent bucket transitions go through `WorkflowService.MoveTask` so preset-defined transition guards remain authoritative (e.g. omakase's `backlog → dev` requires a self-branch comment). Plan auto-finalisation (`plan.done`) is therefore triggered exclusively by the terminal-bucket move, never by claim. | `internal/sqlite/plans.go:ClaimNextPlanTask`, `internal/app/plan_service.go:ClaimNext`, `internal/app/workflow_service.go:MoveTask`, `internal/sqlite/plans.go:MaybeFinalizePlanForTask` |
